extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans, writers, critics, and general readers interested in Norm Macdonald
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and describing the stylistic qualities and techniques that make standup bits (especially Norm Macdonald's) effective — e.g., surprise, long-form digression, deadpan delivery, and anti-humor. Useful for analyzing or composing similar comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: A joke should catch someone by surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: "A joke should catch someone by surprise,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as Norm Macdonald's mission statement: the core aim of a joke is to produce an unexpected result. Use surprise as the primary engine of comedy rather than just predictable setups and payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meandering, straightlaced, anti-humorous setup/path
rubrics_metrics.description: The meandering, straightlaced, sometimes full-on anti-humorous path the joke took to get there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately adopt a straightfaced, slow, or 'anti-humor' tone in the setup so the audience misreads intent and expectation. This style uses apparent aimlessness as a tool rather than a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long shaggy-dog digression that seems to build but doesn't
rubrics_metrics.description: What comes in between is a four-minute shaggy-dog digression ... It makes you think it's going somewhere, and it isn't. It sounds like it's building to something, but it doesn't, not really.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extended, intricate storytelling that mimics narrative momentum but deliberately withholds a conventional payoff. The example (The Moth Joke) shows how length and apparent buildup create a particular kind of comedic expectation to be subverted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aimlessness and disdain for the listener can produce 'funny' via length
rubrics_metrics.description: It is one of those jokes where its aimlessness and disdain for its listener earns 'funny' simply through sheer length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat audience discomfort and mounting confusion as a source of comedy (nervous laughter). This is an intentional technique: the comedian's seeming disregard for a satisfying payoff becomes the joke's engine rather than an error to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained tension then abrupt, small punchline puncture
rubrics_metrics.description: The tension drawn out past the point of being bearable, only to be fully and instantly punctured by the chewing-gum-wrapper punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain narrative tension well beyond normal limits and then resolve it with a minimal, almost anti-climactic punchline. The contrast between long tension and tiny payoff is the source of the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan voice with a barely-suppressed hint of manic delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Something about the voice, and the delivery, and the deadpan-with-a-barely-suppressed-hint-of-manic package elevated all material
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery matters as much as text: a controlled deadpan combined with subtle manic energy can make ordinary or absurd lines land exceptionally well. Work on vocal tone, timing, and micro-expressions to create this effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace of the 'stupid' or dumb punchline as an artistic choice
rubrics_metrics.description: That was Norm: a genius of the stupid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow intentionally simple, dumb, or seemingly lowbrow punchlines when they serve a larger structural or tonal goal. 'Stupid' lines can be artistically sophisticated when they contrast with an elaborate setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material that makes other comedians break indicates quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The guy who said stuff that made other comedians try desperately to keep a straight face, and fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One measure of effectiveness is whether material disrupts the professional composure of peers. If fellow comics are visibly thrown off or break, it signals something unusually strong about the bit's construction or delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planting a memorable, repeatable punchline in listeners' heads
rubrics_metrics.description: What other comedian could have planted a punchline so dumb into the heads of so many people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for lines that stick and are easily recalled/repeated; a successful punchline becomes cultural shorthand. Memorable simplicity can be the mark of a highly effective joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a punchline that completes the yarn, even if dark or personal
rubrics_metrics.description: Maybe that's not the strongest punchline, but it's the only one he ever would have picked to finish off the yarn that came before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select final lines that feel inevitable or fitting for the story you've spun, even if they are dark, blunt, or autobiographical. The appropriateness to the preceding narrative matters more than conventional notions of 'strong' humor.
